transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?
Lately I feel this heavy, empty mood all the time, like I’m weighed down and can’t shake it no matter what I do. It just feels like I'm completely stuck under it and can't get any relief.
How long has this low, empty mood been going on continuously, and have you ever had a similar episode before that fully improved?

This heavy, empty mood has been going on continuously for a little over a year now, starting shortly after I took on those extra night shifts. It has barely let up at all during this time, and I have never experienced an episode like this before in my life.
During this past year, have there been any stretches of at least 2 months when your mood felt back to normal, or has it been low almost every day the whole time?

No, there haven't been any stretches where I felt normal, and it has been low almost every single day this past year. That heavy, empty feeling has pretty much never let up since I started those extra shifts. Even on weeks when the feeling of being watched wasn't as intense, the dark mood was still completely there.
Have you ever had any period of at least 2 months during this time when you felt back to your usual self, or has the low mood been present nearly every day without a long break?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all where I felt back to my usual self. This heavy, numb depression has been there nearly every single day for over a year, ever since I started those extra shifts. It has pretty much never let up.
Have you ever had a period of several days or more when you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or did impulsive things that were out of character?

No, I've never had any times where I felt energized, hyperactive, or irritable like that. It's actually been the exact opposite—I just feel completely heavy, slow, and totally drained of energy all the time. I've never had those kinds of high periods at all.
During this past year, have you also had symptoms like poor sleep, changes in appetite or weight, trouble concentrating, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, or thoughts that life is not worth living?

Yes, my appetite has completely vanished and my pants are hanging off me from losing so much weight. My head also feels incredibly foggy, making it hard to concentrate or make even simple decisions. On the worst days, I even catch myself wishing I wouldn't wake up or thinking about stepping in front of a train on my way home.
Before this past year, had you ever had a long-standing pattern of feeling depressed or down for most of the day, more days than not, for at least 2 years?

No, I didn't have any kind of depression like this before. Before I started taking on those extra night shifts about a year and a half ago, I was actually doing really well, playing soccer and painting murals. This heavy, empty feeling only started after my work schedule changed.
Have you ever had times when you felt especially guilty or worthless, or believed things that others said were not true, such as hearing or seeing things that weren’t there?

I don’t hear or see things that aren't there, but I do believe things that everyone else insists are untrue. I'm convinced the cameras at the hospital and even the mirrors at home are watching me specifically as part of an experiment on my mind. It just makes me feel even more empty inside, like everything is completely pointless.

Have you had any periods of at least 2 weeks where the mood symptoms were present without the belief that you were being watched or experimented on, or do those beliefs only happen when the depression is at its worst?

That heavy, empty depression is pretty much always present and has rarely let up, even during weeks when the thoughts about the cameras back off. On my worst days, both the dark mood and the paranoid thoughts definitely hit me at the same time, but the depression persists even when those thoughts aren't as active.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when the paranoia or beliefs about being watched were present even though your mood was not depressed or empty?

Yes, a few months ago there was a stretch of about two or three weeks where my mood wasn't really sad, just kind of flat. Even though I didn't feel that heavy darkness, I was still completely convinced that the cameras on the unit and the mirrors at home were tracking my thoughts.

Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you felt depressed or empty but did not have the belief that you were being watched or monitored, or do the paranoid beliefs always happen only when the depression is present?

Yes, there have been plenty of times like that. The heavy, empty depression is pretty much constant and never really lets up, even during weeks when the thoughts about the cameras and mirrors fade away. So the low mood is definitely still there even when I don't feel like I'm being watched.
Do you ever hear voices or see things that other people cannot, or have you had any other unusual beliefs besides feeling watched or monitored?

No, I don't hear any voices or see things that aren't there. But I do believe the hospital is running some kind of experiment on my mind and everyone is in on it. I've even had times where I think the colors in my murals are spying on me.
Have the paranoid beliefs ever lasted for at least 2 weeks when your depression was completely absent, or have they only happened during times when you were also depressed?

Yes, a few months ago there was a stretch of about two or three weeks where the heavy depression lifted slightly and I just felt flat rather than intensely sad. Even though the deep depression wasn't really there during that time, I still firmly believed the cameras and mirrors were spying on me and recording my thoughts.
Have you ever had any periods when the paranoia or beliefs that you were being watched were completely absent for several weeks, or do they keep coming back even when your mood is not depressed?

There are times when the thoughts about being watched quiet down for a bit, but they definitely keep coming back even when my mood isn't deeply depressed. Like a few months ago, my mood was just flat for a couple of weeks, but I was still totally convinced the cameras and mirrors were recording my thoughts.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you had no depression or emptiness at all, but the belief that you were being watched or monitored was still clearly present?

Yes, a few months ago there was a stretch of about two weeks or more where that heavy depression and emptiness were gone, and I just felt flat. Even without the dark mood, I was still completely convinced that the cameras and mirrors were watching me and recording my thoughts.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you had no depression or emptiness at all, but the belief that you were being watched or monitored was still clearly present?

Yes, a few months ago there was a stretch of about two weeks or more where that heavy sadness and emptiness lifted a bit, leaving me feeling more flat than depressed. Even without the deep depression, I was still completely convinced that the cameras and mirrors were monitoring and recording my thoughts.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you had no depression or emptiness at all, but the belief that you were being watched or monitored was still clearly present?

Yes, a few months ago there was a period of about two weeks or more where the heavy depression wasn't there and I just felt flat. Even during that time without the low mood, I remained completely convinced that the unit cameras and my mirrors at home were set up to watch me and record my thoughts.
Have you ever had any period of at least 2 weeks when the depression was gone and you felt back to normal, while the belief that you were being watched was still clearly present?

No, I wouldn't say I felt completely back to normal, my mood was just flat and empty rather than deeply sad. But during those two weeks, I was still absolutely convinced that the cameras at work and the mirrors at home were set up to watch me and read my thoughts.

Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you felt completely back to normal emotionally, with no depression or emptiness at all, while still believing the cameras or mirrors were watching you?

No, I wouldn't say I felt completely back to normal, but rather my mood was just flat or neutral instead of deeply sad. During those two weeks, that heavy depression and sadness had lifted, yet I was still completely convinced the cameras on the unit and the mirrors at home were watching me and recording my thoughts.

Have you ever had any period of at least 2 weeks when you felt completely back to your usual self emotionally, with no depression or emptiness at all, while still believing the cameras or mirrors were watching you?

No, I didn't feel completely back to my old self, but there was a stretch a few months ago for about two weeks where the depression and emptiness were gone and I just felt flat. Even though that low mood was gone, I was still absolutely convinced that the cameras on the unit and the mirrors at home were watching me and recording my thoughts.

No, I didn't feel completely back to my usual self, because my mood was just flat rather than happy or normal. But during those two weeks, even though that heavy sadness was gone, I was still absolutely convinced the cameras and mirrors were watching me and recording my thoughts.

No, I have never heard any voices or seen things that weren't there, even when my mood wasn't low. But during that flat period a few months ago when I wasn't feeling depressed, I still strongly believed that the cameras and mirrors were watching me and tracking my thoughts.

Yes, they do continue even when I'm not feeling depressed. A few months ago, I had a stretch of about two weeks or more where I didn't feel that heavy sadness, just flat, but I still firmly believed the cameras and mirrors were watching me and recording my thoughts.

Have you ever had hallucinations or fixed beliefs like the cameras or mirrors watching you for at least 2 weeks when you were not depressed or empty at all?

Yes, a few months ago there was a stretch of about two weeks or more where my mood felt flat but not particularly sad or empty. Yet, during that time, I was still completely convinced that the cameras and mirrors were part of a setup to read and record my thoughts.
